metadata.title: AI Evaluation: How Do You Know Your AI Product Is Good?

beats.narration_text: Hello, I'm Vineet S.. Anyone can make an A I demo look good. The hard part is knowing whether it is actually good, and whether a new model is safe to ship. That is what evaluation is for. Here is how product managers do it.

props.segment: AI Evaluation: How Do You Know Your AI Product Is Good?
props.command: How do I know my AI product is good?
output: Test on real cases, not demos
Ship only when it beats the last release

beats.narration_text: An AI product is good when it passes real tests, release after release. A demo shows one good moment. Evaluation shows how often it is good, and whether it stays good when anything changes.

props.text:
An AI product is good
when the demo
looks impressive.
props.replacementWords: it passes real tests, release after release

beats.narration_text: Here are the tools. A golden dataset. Test cases. Human evaluation. L L M as a judge. Regression testing. And the launch decision. Together they answer one question: is this version better than the last, and good enough to ship?

props.caption: Better than the last, and good enough?

beats.narration_text: Start with a golden dataset: real questions paired with answers that experts agree are correct. Break it into test cases, where each case checks one behavior. Cover the edges, meaning rare, tricky and risky inputs, not only the easy ones. And keep the set fixed and private, so teams cannot tune to it.

layers.title: Test cases
layers.sub: Each one checks a single behavior

layers.title: Keep it fixed and private
layers.sub: So nobody can tune to the test

beats.narration_text: Human evaluation is the gold standard. Reviewers read answers and score them against a rubric, for example accuracy, tone and safety. The rubric matters most. If two reviewers disagree about what a good answer is, the scores mean little. So agree on the rubric first, and have more than one person score.

L L M as a judge means a second model scores the first one's answers against your rubric. It scales to thousands of answers, which humans cannot. But judges have biases, such as favoring longer answers. So treat the judge as a measuring instrument, and calibrate it by comparing its scores with human scores.

layers.title: How it works
layers.sub: Give it the rubric and the answer

layers.title: The catch
layers.sub: It has biases, like favoring long answers

layers.title: Calibrate it
layers.sub: Compare its scores with human scores

beats.narration_text: Regression testing asks: did we break something that used to work? Re-run the same test set whenever anything changes. A prompt edit, a model upgrade, new data, or a change in retrieval. A new model that is better on average can still be worse on cases you care about, so compare case by case.

So is a new model ready? Ask four questions. Does it beat the current version on the golden set, case by case? Does it avoid new critical failures, especially on safety and high-stakes cases? Do cost and speed fit the budget? And can you roll it out gradually, with a rollback ready? If any answer is no, it is not ready.

layers.title: Beats the current one
layers.sub: On the golden set, case by case

beats.narration_text: So, evaluation. Build a golden dataset. Score with humans and a calibrated judge. Re-run tests on every change. And ship only when the new version earns it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. I am a product manager about to ship an AI feature that does this: [describe it]. Help me build an evaluation plan: ten golden test cases including three hard edge cases, a four-part human rubric, how I would use an LLM judge and check it, the regression tests I should run on every change, and the launch criteria for a new model. Then tell me which evaluation step I am most likely to skip. The last sentence is the useful one. Teams skip the same step again and again, usually regression testing, so look at what Claude says you are likely to skip, and do that one first. Pause here and run it on your own product.
